findings.description: The early-return shortcut returns max(max(0, self.min), self.max), whereas the original formula was max(max(0, min), min(result, max)). When min > max the shortcut returns min, which matches the original, so that case is fine. But the shortcut is only taken if exponent > log(max/multiplier); the original computes min(result, max), which with result > max gives max, so the result is the same. This looks equivalent, so the flagged concern is limited to float precision at the boundary.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the exponent is slightly above log(max/multiplier) but floating-point error makes the check imprecise, e.g. result is only marginally below max. The shortcut then returns max where the original would return result. The difference is negligible, so the practical impact is minimal.
